doc.title: Bill Crow interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 18, 1995

title: A new story about Gene Bertoncini and goodbyes
summary: He tells a story of Gene Bertoncini and Bobby Shanken, then the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: It’s like saying pick a favorite tune. You know I just, I really can’t do that. I always loved the one I’m involved in at the moment. I’ll give you a new story that’s not in there. Gene Bertoncini was chatting up a girl on the street while he was waiting for Bobby Shanken to come down, the drummer. And Gene is a very handsome guy and beautifully dressed usually, and very tidy. And when he told her that he was a guitar player, she didn’t believe him. She said, “You don’t look like a guitar player.” She’s thinking of rock guitar players. So Bobby comes down, and he says, “Bobby, would you explain to this young lady how I make my living?” And Bobby says, “Well, he’s one of the best jazz players in the world, and I have no idea how he makes his living.”
Good one. All right. Well thanks for your time.
It’s been a real pleasure. © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-
